I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have six properties and $453 cash. I just bought Connecticut Avenue. Player one has $649 and owns Vermont, Electric, St James, Tennessee, Indiana, Water Works, and Marvin Gardens.

Player one holds the full orange set: St. James, Tennessee, and Indiana. I own Connecticut Avenue, which completes the light blue group.

Player one owns both utilities. He has two of the three orange properties and one of the three red ones. He does not yet own New York.

Player three has $655 and owns Reading RR, St. Charles, Pennsylvania RR, Illinois, and Short Line. Player four has $1488 and owns only Boardwalk. Park Place is still unowned. New York is also unowned.

No monopolies exist yet, so building is impossible. I cannot trade for Pennsylvania Avenue because it is unowned. Completing the light blue set would require both Oriental and Vermont, which are unavailable. I will likely end my turn without trading.

Player three wants B&O, but selling it would let them collect $200 in rent from four railroads. Player one cannot complete the orange set through trade because New York is unowned. I am now weighing whether trading my green properties for something better is worthwhile.

Player one previously rejected an orange swap. He will not trade his orange set. Player four has Boardwalk and $1488 cash, but he likely has no interest in swapping.

I am now considering trading for Vermont from player one. That would give me two of the three light blue properties, but Oriental is still unowned and anyone could land there. Light blue houses cost only fifty dollars each, so the return on investment would be high.

Player one previously rejected cash for Indiana, so he likely wants trade chips rather than money. Offering Mediterranean Avenue plus cash for Vermont would not be attractive, since that property is nearly worthless. Trading Ventnor for Marvin would not complete the yellow set either. I am now weighing whether to end my turn without trading, given that I already hold a solid position with two-thirds of the green group and a railroads blocker.

I have ruled out every trade that could complete a monopoly, since the missing pieces are all unowned. I am now reconsidering player three as a possible trading partner.

I am now considering giving B&O to player four instead of player three. That would leave player three with only three railroads, but player four could still flip the property for a premium. Player one offers no useful trade to weaken player three's path.

Selling Mediterranean Avenue would yield only thirty dollars in cash, so that idea is dismissed. I will end my turn without trading and hold my current blockers. I am now considering whether to propose a trade that might be profitable even if it does not complete a set.

I am now calculating whether buying Vermont from player one is worthwhile. I would trade Mediterranean Avenue plus cash for it. That leaves me with two of the three light blue properties, though Oriental remains unowned. The cash cost would reduce my balance, but B&O mortgage value covers the remaining gap to buy Pennsylvania Avenue.

Player one would likely demand a premium for Vermont, since it completes my light blue set. I am now considering giving Ventnor to player one instead. That would let them reach two-thirds of the yellow group, but they still need Atlantic to finish it. I currently block them from that position.

A swap of Ventnor for Vermont would give me two-thirds of the light blue set. Oriental is only one hundred dollars, so it is cheap to finish. Yellow is more expensive at two hundred sixty dollars. Light blue houses cost fifty dollars each, which is a better return on investment. This trade might be profitable even though both properties are still unowned.

Three houses on the light blue set would cost four hundred fifty dollars and yield eight hundred forty dollars in rent per hit. Player one has only six hundred forty-nine dollars, so he cannot afford three houses on every yellow property immediately.

I can almost fully build the light blue set with my current cash, but I would need to buy Oriental first and still have only about seven houses left. The swap would not complete either set. It would improve my odds for the better return on investment while giving player one a chance at yellow. I think it is mildly positive expected value, though player one might not accept it.

I am weighing whether to propose the trade. Player one would lose his light-blue blocker and gain Ventnor for his yellow group. I am unsure if this swap is worth the risk. I also need to check how post-turn actions resolve.

I am unsure whether proposing a trade blocks further post-turn actions until the response is received. I will proceed with a reasonable offer if it has positive expected value.

Player four has no interest in cash. Selling Connecticut Avenue to him would give him a light blue foothold, which is dangerous if he later acquires Oriental and Vermont. Extra cash would not help without a completed monopoly.

Player one previously rejected an offer for Indiana to keep it as a chip for New York. Player three wants the fourth railroad, so I will not give it to them. A swap of my two-thirds green group for player one's two-thirds orange group would be more valuable than the previous attempt, since orange is cheaper to build and New York is only two hundred dollars while Pennsylvania Avenue is three hundred twenty.

I will end my turn without trading. I will not mortgage any properties. I will post a short public message and keep my private notes to the essentials.

messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

your_private_thoughts_last_10.thought: p2 is offering Mediterranean ($60, weak 2-property Brown group) straight up for Vermont ($100, much stronger 3-property Light Blue group). This is a pure downgrade for me with zero upside. Rejecting immediately.

p3 already owns Reading and Pennsylvania Railroads and has $1235 cash. Giving p3 a third railroad ($100 rent on 3 board spaces) for only $300 ($100 profit over list) is bad value for me and strengthens a cash-rich opponent. Better to hold Short Line as a blocker and trade chip for future color sets.

Buying Tennessee Avenue ($180) gives me my second Orange property alongside St. James Place, with New York Avenue still unowned in the bank. Leaves me with $426 cash and puts me one property away from the best monopoly on the board.

I now hold 2 Oranges (St. James Place and Tennessee Avenue) with New York Avenue still unowned, plus $426 cash and 5 other properties. No trades can complete any sets yet, so I'll end my turn and preserve cash for upcoming unowned properties.

p3 just offered p2 $400 cash for a third railroad, and Water Works is a dead single for p3 since I own Electric Company. Getting the Utility pair (10x dice roll) plus extra cash to fund my Orange monopoly chase and upcoming unowned properties is great for me, especially since p2 and p4 will also take the hit from p3's 3 railroads. I'll counter at $300 + Water Works for Short Line.

Paid $25 rent on B&O Railroad. I have $701 cash, the Utility monopoly, 2 Oranges (with New York Ave still unowned), and 3 other properties. No color sets can be completed via trade yet since all remaining deeds in those groups are still unowned. Ending turn.

p2 is offering 2 Greens (Pacific and North Carolina, $200/house) for my 2 Oranges (St. James and Tennessee, $100/house). Oranges are far superior to Greens in both landing frequency and development cost, especially with my $701 cash stack. Rejecting immediately.

p3 already holds 3 Railroads and Illinois Avenue. Selling Indiana Avenue for $300 would put p3 one unowned deed (Kentucky) away from a devastating Red monopoly while giving away my best trade chip for New York Avenue. I already have $701 cash and can't build on Oranges until New York is bought anyway. Rejecting.
